title: Indonesia Quake Kills 47 as Trump Vows to Declare Hormuz US Territory, China-Philippines Clash in South China Sea
subhead: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Indonesia's Flores region, killing at least 47, while President Trump said he will 'soon' declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory and a new China-Philippines clash injured a Filipino sailor at a disputed shoal.

sections.heading: Magnitude 7.7 Quake Hits Indonesia's Flores Region
sections.body:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off Indonesia's coast early Saturday, killing at least 47 people and toppling buildings, according to the US Geological Survey and the Indonesian National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS). The quake hit the Flores region at a depth of 10 kilometers, with its epicenter 68 km (42 miles) north-northwest of the city of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province, and was followed by several aftershocks. AP reports rescuers clearing debris in Maumere and residents evacuating to higher ground in East Manggarai.

The death toll is expected to rise as search-and-rescue operations continue across the affected islands. Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and is frequently hit by major earthquakes, but the shallow depth and proximity to populated coastal towns in East Nusa Tenggara made this one particularly destructive.
sections.whyItMatters: A major humanitarian disaster in a region already strained by years of natural disasters; the shallow quake's coastal location raises the risk of landslides and a possible tsunami threat, and the toll is likely to climb.

sections.heading: Trump Says He Will Declare Hormuz a US Territory
sections.body:
President Donald Trump said he will 'soon' declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory, according to Al Jazeera, which noted that the comments overstate the level of US control over the international shipping route. The declaration would mark a sharp escalation in the US-Iran conflict, effectively asserting a territorial claim over a waterway that carries a large share of global oil trade and that Iran has largely closed since the war began in late February.

The move comes as the US Navy pulls its last aircraft carrier out of the Pacific. AP reports the USS George Washington is departing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East, whose deployment has been extended from its original May return date amid concerns about mental health and supply issues aboard the long-deployed carrier. Analysts cited by AP said the open-ended operations against Iran are running American sailors ragged while the administration focuses on the Western Hemisphere.
sections.whyItMatters: A unilateral US territorial claim over an international strait would be a major legal and diplomatic rupture, and the carrier redeployment leaves the western Pacific without a US carrier just as China shows more assertiveness in the region.

sections.heading: China-Philippines Clash at Second Thomas Shoal
sections.body:
The Philippine military accused China's coast guard of injuring a Filipino sailor during an incident at the disputed Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea, AP reports. The military said Chinese coast guard personnel aboard a motorboat repeatedly struck the sailor on the head with a wooden baton, injuring him and damaging his smaller vessel, in an assault captured on video. China's coast guard countered that two rubber boats from an 'illegally' stationed Filipino vessel had rammed its patrol boat, and that Philippine personnel attacked its officers with oars and long sticks.

The clash is the latest in a series of altercations around the rusting BRP Sierra Madre, a long-marooned Philippine navy ship that serves as a territorial outpost and that Beijing has demanded Manila remove. Separately, Taiwan's opposition-controlled parliament approved a $93 billion annual budget late Friday after a record 266 days of deadlock, preserving funding for a drone programme central to the island's defence plans against China, according to Al Jazeera.
sections.whyItMatters: The South China Sea incident and Taiwan's budget approval both come as the US carrier absence from the Pacific raises questions about Washington's ability to reassure allies in the region.

sections.heading: Israeli Strikes Kill 11 in Southern Lebanon
sections.body:
Israeli air strikes killed at least 11 people and wounded 19 in southern Lebanon, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Health, as attacks intensified across several towns overnight. Al Jazeera reports that strikes on Ansar and Deir ez-Zahrani in Nabatieh district killed seven (including three children) and four people respectively. Hezbollah issued a statement urging the Lebanese government to abandon what it called 'humiliating' direct negotiations and to stop relying on US mediation, warning that the Israeli attacks would be met with an 'appropriate response'.

Lebanon's parliament speaker Nabih Berri called the attacks a 'massacre' and said they represented the continuation of a 'war aimed at extermination' in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military said it had struck what it described as Hezbollah targets, according to Al Jazeera.
sections.whyItMatters: The strikes threaten to unravel the fragile ceasefire and the US-mediated border talks that Lebanon had described as making 'positive progress' just over a week ago, and Hezbollah's rejection of direct negotiations signals a hardening of positions.

sections.heading: Erdogan Says Egypt Could Join Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Defence Pact
sections.body:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said Egypt could join the joint defence agreement recently signed by Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, describing Cairo's accession as 'possible' and the pact as open to further members, in an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera. The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed last Friday by Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, commits signatories to unified steps should any one of them come under external attack, a collective-deterrence provision analysts have compared to NATO's Article 5.

Erdogan also said reopening the Strait of Hormuz was a priority for Ankara, arguing its continued closure served no one's interests, and credited Qatar with playing an important role in mediation efforts. He pledged Turkey would not leave Syria, Gaza and Lebanon to face regional turmoil alone.
sections.whyItMatters: Expanding the Mecca Pact to include Egypt would significantly broaden a new Middle East security bloc at a time when the US-Iran war and Hormuz closure are reshaping regional alignments.

sections.heading: Ukraine Strikes Russian Satellite-Internet Network
sections.body:
Ukraine used domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles to strike targets in Russia's southwestern Samara region, hitting a military airfield and a rocket centre that supports Russia's Starlink-style satellite internet network, according to Al Jazeera. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes hit the Progress Centre rocket facility for Russia's space agency Roscosmos, about 900 km (560 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and the Savasleyka air base about 700 km away. The mayor of Samara, Ivan Noskov, said air defences had repelled a 'massive' attack and that some industrial sites had been damaged.

Meanwhile, Moscow is demanding answers from Washington and Ankara about a potential plan to send Kyiv a 'substantial arsenal' of US weapons and ammunition held by Turkey, Al Jazeera reports. Russia also struck an apartment block in the southeastern town of Marhanets, where a three-month-old baby was killed.
sections.whyItMatters: Ukraine's long-range strikes deep into Russia, including against satellite-communications infrastructure, show Kyiv's growing domestic strike capability even as Moscow presses Washington and Ankara over a potential transfer of US-held weapons from Turkey.

bottomLine: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake killed at least 47 in Indonesia's Flores region, while President Trump escalated the Iran conflict by vowing to declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory and pulled the last US carrier out of the Pacific. In Asia, a new China-Philippines clash at Second Thomas Shoal and Taiwan's passage of a $93 billion defence budget underscored the region's unease over the US focus shifting away from the Pacific. In the Middle East, Israeli strikes killed 11 in southern Lebanon as Hezbollah rejected US-mediated talks, and Erdogan floated Egypt joining the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Mecca Pact. Ukraine struck deep into Russia's Samara region, hitting satellite-communications infrastructure, as Moscow pressed Washington and Ankara over a potential transfer of US-held weapons from Turkey. The day's through-line: a US stretched between the Iran war and the Western Hemisphere is leaving vacuums and raising questions across the Pacific and the Middle East alike.
